observation.visible_scene: A static night cityscape dominated by the tall, segmented Taipei 101 tower at center, illuminated in teal/green with a bright blue-lit crown and spire. To its right stands a slimmer skyscraper topped with magenta/purple lighting, and to the left a blocky building with a red-lit upper edge; a dense foreground of lit residential and office towers fills the lower third. A thick layer of low cloud/fog hangs across the upper half of the frame, backlit by the city glow.
visible_changes: The cloud/fog layer drifts across the sky over the excerpt, periodically sliding in front of the top of the central tower.

The blue-lit crown/spire of the central tower is visible at the start (frames 1-7), becomes obscured by passing cloud from roughly frame 8 through frame 38, and re-emerges clearly in the final frames (39-41).
Red aviation-obstruction lights on the right-hand skyscraper blink on and off between frames (e.g., present in frames 1, 5-6, 14-16, 20, 29-30, 35-37, absent in others) rather than moving.
The skyline, building positions, and the steady colored facade lighting (teal center, magenta right, red left, scattered window lights) remain constant throughout.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the cloud drift had a defined start or end outside this segment; the excerpt captures it already in progress and still continuing at the cut boundaries.
uncertain_details: The exact horizontal direction of the cloud motion is hard to pin down frame-to-frame; only the intermittent occlusion of the tower top is clearly supported.
Camera is treated as static because building positions do not shift, but a very small fixed-camera framing cannot be fully ruled out.
The blinking red dots are interpreted as obstruction lights, not as separate moving objects.
